clinician.final_diagnosis: Metastatic malignant melanoma from anorectal primary to breast
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old woman presented in February 2019 with intermittent blood in stool for 2 months. Abdominal CT revealed a thickened and eccentric lesion in the lower rectum-anal canal area with local lumen constriction and enlarged surrounding lymph nodes. Surgical resection of the anorectal tumor and histology confirmed anorectal malignant melanoma. Immunohistochemistry of the anorectal tumor showed positivity for melanoma markers HMB-45, Melan-A, S100, and Vimentin, and negativity for PCK and P16. Twenty-nine months later, a breast lesion was identified and removed by modified radical mastectomy. Immunohistochemical staining of the breast lesion was positive for the same melanoma markers and negative for epithelial and other markers (CK, CK7, CD34, WT-1), supporting that it was a metastasis of the primary anorectal malignant melanoma.
